Gate | Demotion gate: live -> paper (HARD — automatic) | gen

Trigger A — signal decay | rolling 250-bet closing-line-value lower bound < 0 at two consecutive monthly evaluations, OR signal ROI below break-even over the trailing 150 settled bets with the one-sided test p > 0.5 (indistinguishable from losing) | gen
Trigger B — risk breach | drawdown from live peak exceeds 50% of allocated bankroll at live stakes, OR stake cap exceeded, OR a ledger audit invalidates settled results (source correction) | gen
Trigger C — compliance | any G-12 failure (prohibited market class, unregistered input, non-public information) — immediate, no evaluation window | gen
Destination | PAPER (Stage 2 exposure): zero capital, sealed evaluation continues, the entry keeps its record and its graveyard rights | gen
Execution | automatic at the evaluation checkpoint by the system; no discretion, no appeal; the demotion event is written to the strategy's sealed log | gen

Re-entry | back through the normal ladder from paper: a fresh sealed window of >= 150 settled paper bets with positive CLV lower bound AND all hard gates re-cleared on that window; a demoted strategy may not re-enter live on the strength of its old record | gen
Asymmetry | staking outcomes can NEVER promote (promotion reads signal columns only), but a staking risk breach CAN demote. A lucky staking run masks nothing; a dangerous one is punished. | gen

Why | The failure mode of every strategy programme is the edge that died quietly while the bankroll looked fine. G-11 monitors decay; G-16 is the enforcement: the strategy stops carrying capital the moment the evidence stops supporting it. | gen
